The Perfect Setting. For Life.
‍
Senoia is the perfect setting for living, and for business and commerce!
‍
‍
The historic downtown Senoia area is a thriving small business community featuring restaurants, bars, boutiques, hair and nail stylists, dentists, doctors, furniture, antiques, and more, all in our walkable downtown and historic residential district.
‍
Our downtown has grown dramatically in recent years with an influx of new businesses, yet retains that small-town look and feel and, above all, the friendliness and hospitality Senoia is known for.
‍
There is always something going on in Senoia, from the Farmer's Market on Saturdays to Alive After Five, a monthly celebration featuring vendors, entertainment, music, and fun for the whole family. The Light Up Senoia Christmas parade is a holiday tradition, as is our Memorial Day parade and events. Our 2nd Annual PorchFest earlier this year was a huge success, something we're already looking forward to for next year. The Annual Senoia Car show is, quite literally, world-famous, drawing classic car enthusiasts from around the SouthEast and beyond. And there's more....
‍
The Senoia Downtown Development Authority organizes and supports wholesome, family-friendly events for our visitors, residents, and future residents. Our guests see first-hand the charm and hospitality that has brought so many new people and businesses to Senoia.
‍
Senoia truly is the perfect setting for life. We invite you to come and see for yourself!

The mission of the Senoia DDA is to revitalize, enhance, promote, and stimulate the economic development of Senoia while maintaining its historical integrity and charm.
More
DDA Board
Small Business Heritage
The Senoia Downtown Development Authority (DDA) is a public body created by the City of Senoia. Our purpose is economic development through downtown revitalization, heritage, preservation, and restoration of an historic sense of place. The Senoia DDA is an independent authority dedicated to the revitalization and promotion of all commercially zoned areas in the city limits of Senoia.

DDA Committees
‍
Organization:
Builds consensus and cooperation among the many groups and individuals who have a stake in the revitalization process. Provides a forum for many different groups and individuals to work together for the shared goal of thriving business districts. Meets on an as-needed basis.
‍
Design:
Promotes the rehabilitation of existing buildings in order to create an attractive commercial center, while paying attention to all physical attributes in and around downtown and all other commercial areas. Meets third Tuesday of every month at 9:00am at the Senoia Welcome Center.
‍
Economic Restructuring:
Examines the existing business mix of downtown and works first to enhance the existing business community through retention, expansion and recruitment of new businesses to strengthen the city’s economic base. Meets 3rd Thursday of every month at 7:00pm at the Senoia Welcome Center.
‍
Promotions:
Promotes downtown through quality events and marketing that will attract people into the downtown area of the city to shop, work, and invest. Meets 1st Thursday of the month at 9:00 am at Senoia Welcome Center. Email Stephanie Reeder at georgiareeders@yahoo.com for more information.
‍
Subcommittees include the Cultural Arts subcommittee, which focuses on bringing art, music, literature, theater, and film to the city. Meets 1st Thursday of the month at 9:00am at Senoia Welcome Center. Email Stephanie Reeder at georgiareeders@yahoo.com for more information. Subcommittees also include Senoia Alive After Five, which focuses on shopping, dining, and family-friendly entertainment downtown. The Alive After Five Comittee meets on an as needed basis. Please email aliveafter5senoia@gmail.com for more information.
‍

Senoia History
In the Beginning…‍
‍
Coweta County (pronounced “Cow-eeta” or “Ky-eeta” & meaning “water falls”) was formed in Georgia in June 9, 1825 as Chief William McIntosh signed the Treaty of Indian Springs, for which he was soon killed by his fellow Creek Indians. Settlers migrated to the area following the Fifth Land Lottery of 1827. Gerrard M. Veal, a minor, received land lot 279, the 202.5 acres that became present day Senoia.
‍
Around 1828, a large number of people traveled from Newberry, South Carolina, in covered wagons, oxcarts, on horseback, and by foot.  In the group were preachers, farmers, masons, and most any other occupation of the day. The names read like a current register of the area, since these forerunners have numerous descendants still making their homes in Senoia.  In the group from South Carolina were the Atkinsons, Addys, Pages, Youngs, Levells, Shells, Barnes, Falls, Moses and many others. They scattered across the countryside, each trying to find a new start. And find it they did in the rich land of eastern Coweta. Raising cotton, corn, and livestock, the area was an agricultural Utopia.
‍
‍
Location, Location, Location…
‍
The first “settlement” in the area was called Location, two miles south of present day Senoia, where a post office had been established.   In 1854, Willow Dell was established.  Settlers continued to move to the area.  The founding date for Senoia is 1860, for in that year the Rev. Francis Warren Baggarly bought land on which the modern town of Senoia now sits.  On October 9, 1864, after many of the people of Willow Dell had moved closer to the two railroads that ran through the area, the community was renamed Senoia, and a post office was reestablished.  The first building to be erected was known as the Rock House. Intended for mercantile purposes, it soon became a commissary for the Confederacy, as the war broke out soon after its completion. The first church, a Methodist Episcopal, with the Rev. Baggarly as minister, and the first Sunday school was also organized in the upstairs.   A high school was opened in 1865, quite an accomplishment for a rural southern town at the end of the civil war. Two intersecting railroads are much of the reason that Senoia is located where it is.
Pictured is the old depot, which no longer stands
‍
Post Civil War
After the war, Senoia saw the completion of the Savannah, Griffin and North Alabama Railroad, which crossed through the town.   Agricultural products such as cotton and peaches were shipped by rail from Senoia.  Senoia was officially incorporated as a city on December 12, 1866. Pride in their town was very evident, as the citizens aspired to have the county seat moved there in 1876. Their bid was unsuccessful. Today with its collection of architectural treasures, most of the town comprises a historic district on the National Register of Historic Places.  Senoia was officially chartered as a city around 1905, about the same time the railways moved in. The city still features architecture from all those periods – including structures dating to the 1840s – with most of the architecture from the city’s charming downtown dating from the turn of the century.
Senoia has one known citizen who died in combat. Edward Couch was killed in action in Vietnam. The city of Senoia honored its lone fallen hero by naming its newest bridge in his honor in 2001.
Where the name Senoia came from is difficult to determine.  There are four main variations to the origins of the name Senoia.  They are listed below in the order of their likelihood as the source for the name Senoia:
‍
Senoya He-ne-ha was the wife of Captain William McIntosh.  Their son, also named William McIntosh was both a General in the army and a chief in his band of Creek Indians. Senoya was a member of the prestigious Wind Clan of the Creek Indians.  This is what established the idea of “Princess Senoia.”
From an edition of a one-time Senoia paper, the Enterprise-Gazette, comes this quotation concerning the naming of the town:  “John Williams suggested the name Senoia for an Indian Chief of that name, a medicine man and philanthropist, noble, brave, and generous, who lived near the present location of Sargent.
Another newspaper account in 1873 held that Colonel William C. Barnes came up with the name in honor of a clever Indian who formerly resided in the community.
Others say that Senoia comes from an Indian word for the title of Chief William McIntosh, Shenoywa.
Another thing for visitors to Senoia to note:  Although you might think that Senoia would most likely be pronounced “Seh-noy-yuh”, don’t be fooled.  Locals here simply call it “Seh-noy.”  If you want to stand out like a sore thumb, feel free to mispronounce Senoia.  No one will say anything, but every one will know you are not a “local”!
‍
‍

The Perfect Setting. For Life.
‍
Senoia is the perfect setting for living, and for business and commerce!
‍
‍
The historic downtown Senoia area is a thriving small business community featuring restaurants, bars, boutiques, hair and nail stylists, dentists, doctors, furniture, antiques, and more, all in our walkable downtown and historic residential district.
‍
Our downtown has grown dramatically in recent years with an influx of new businesses, yet retains that small-town look and feel and, above all, the friendliness and hospitality Senoia is known for.
‍
There is always something going on in Senoia, from the Farmer's Market on Saturdays to Alive After Five, a monthly celebration featuring vendors, entertainment, music, and fun for the whole family. The Light Up Senoia Christmas parade is a holiday tradition, as is our Memorial Day parade and events. Our 2nd Annual PorchFest earlier this year was a huge success, something we're already looking forward to for next year. The Annual Senoia Car show is, quite literally, world-famous, drawing classic car enthusiasts from around the SouthEast and beyond. And there's more....
‍
The Senoia Downtown Development Authority organizes and supports wholesome, family-friendly events for our visitors, residents, and future residents. Our guests see first-hand the charm and hospitality that has brought so many new people and businesses to Senoia.
‍
Senoia truly is the perfect setting for life. We invite you to come and see for yourself!

Event Overview:
Get ready to celebrate the most wonderful time of the year at our annual Light Up Senoia Parade! This cherished tradition brings the community together for an evening of festivities and Christmas cheer! Parade begins promptly at 6:30pm. This is a wonderful way to promote your business and have some holiday fun!
Event Highlights:
Festive Floats by local businesses, schools, churches, and organizations
Dance Groups
Cheerful Music & Holiday Entertainment
Food Trucks
Santa Claus
Santa's Workshop
Main Street Tree Lighting
Awards & Trophies
& More!
Event Schedule:
4:00pm: Santa's Workshop Opens! Located at the Senoia Farmers' Market, 40 Travis Street
‍4:15pm: Pre parade entertainment begins in front of the stage on Main Street
‍4:30pm-5:30pm: Check in for parade participants (further details below)
‍6:00pm: Santa's Workshop Closes, making your way towards Main Street for the parade!
‍6:30pm: PARADE BEGINS
‍The Light Up Senoia tree lighting will immediately follow the parade. And then Santa will receive visitors on his sleigh until 8:30.
‍
REGISTER TO SUBMIT AN ENTRY IN THE PARADE
The theme for this year’s parade is “Christmas Through the Decades". All parade entries will be judged with the theme as the basis for trophy awards. The following category winners will receive a trophy.
Mayor’s trophy (best overall entry)
Grand Marshal’s trophy (best creative entry)
Santa’s trophy (best Christmas Spirit)
Rudolph’s trophy (best lighted entry)
Reindeer trophy (best musical/vocal/dance entry)
With it being nighttime,
we encourage lights
! It will be dark when the parade starts, so use those LIGHTS!!! (You will supply all electricity for your entry) Be creative! Please have some type of banner in front of your entry announcing your group's name.
You
CAN NOT have a SANTA on your float
, Santa will be at the end of the parade on the his Fire Truck.
Please
…
no items can be thrown from parade participants
! You may have someone
walking beside your entry to hand out candy, beads etc. This is for the safety of the children. Thank you for your cooperation
.
‍
There is a $20 fee for each parade entry.
‍
CHECK IN TIME FOR PARADE PARTICIPANTS BEGINS AT 4:30 AND ENDS AT 5:30!
‍
You will receive multiple emails the week of the parade that will give you all information you need to know beforehand. Please make sure the email you use on the entry form is monitored, AND please put
info@enjoysenoia.com
in your contact list so your instructions don’t end up in your junk file.
Entries are limited. Sign up NOW!
If you have questions about the parade please email:
lightupsenoia@enjoysenoia.com

/news/senoias-business-of-the-month.text:
Senoia's Business of the Month
Share this
We would like to congratulate the Downtown Senoia Business of the Month, Maguire's Irish Pub.
‍
Maguires Family and Friends restaurant and Irish Pub opened its doors on St. Patrick’s Day 2008.
Owned by Frank and Wendy Maguire, working along side their three children, they are now in their second generation of this true family business. It is their mission to honor their heritage by always providing the great food, great fun, and great service upon which their Grandmother and Grandfather prided themselves.
Maguires has a menu that can make anyone happy, from Fish and Chips, to Cottage Pie, and have you had the Reuben Spring Rolls? ( My personal favorite).  Their drink menu also has something for everyone, with a nice variety of beer and wine, and their handrafted cocktails such as the Irish Old Fashioned.
Happy Hour is daily from 2-6pm, where you can choose from discounted appetizers, and $4 house wines and cocktails, and select draft beer specials.
All of Senoia looks forward to the St. Patrick’s Day Shenanigans, and Maguires does not disappoint! This year the fun begins on Saturday, with Kegs and Eggs at 8am, and finishing the day with a performance by the Kelly Porter Irish Dancers at 6pm. The fun continues into Sunday, and then Monday is the big day, beginning at 8am, with events all day!
Downtown Senoia is fortunate to have such a great establishment that truly cares about its customers and their experience.

Lisa's Crêperie was first created in May 2017. Her passion for French cooking and particularly Crêpes originated when she was just a child. Lisa was born in Nice, France, then raised in the island of Corsica, where she first learned how to make crêpes. Her authentic recipe has been in her family for generations.
In 1997, Lisa relocated to the US where she finished school and went on the join the US Navy as a Helicopter Mechanic, based in San Diego, CA. Every chance she had, Lisa would try crepes to get a little taste of her childhood, but they never tasted like real French Crêpes. While stationed in San Diego, Lisa would make French Crêpes on occasional Friday mornings, to help raise money for her Squadrons Christmas Party funding. It was immediately a huge hit, and all of the officers and enlisted lined up at the door, anxious to get a taste! The delicious smell coming from down the street was simply irresistible! Once out of the Navy, Lisa participated in a French Pop-up event in Princeton, NJ, and Lisa's Crêperie was born.
Lisa and her family relocated to Atlanta, GA and she started serving her delicious french crêpes at the Peachtree City Farmers, private events, festivals and movie sets in and around Atlanta. 2 years later, she opened her first store front at 48 Main St, in Senoia GA and transformed into Lisa's Crêperie & Café.

The Senoia Area Historical Society (SAHS) is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the social and cultural history of Senoia
Map
The Senoia Area Historical Society (SAHS) is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the social and cultural history of Senoia, Georgia and its surrounding community.
Senoia Area Historical Society’s (SAHS) offices and museum are housed in the 1870 Carmichael house located at 6 Couch Street in the Historic District of Senoia, Georgia.  The SAHS continues to work to preserve one of the oldest and most historic homes in Senoia.
In 2016, the Society held a Capital Campaign in which proceeds were used to replace the roof as well as shore up the foundation and repair the floor.   In 2018, SAHS repaired the porch, porch ceiling, as well as return the railings and posts to their original design and beauty, thanks to a matching $10,000 grant from the General Daniel Newnan Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution.

The phrase "Small Town Charm Meets Big City Design" on The Lighting Studio's sign tells Susan Erwin's story in a nutshell.
After spending over twenty years working in Atlanta with engineers, architects, and interior designers on custom lighting design for major construction projects, Susan and her husband, Mike, have moved to the charming town of Senoia, Georgia and opened a lighting design studio and showroom that combines small town charm with big city design.
In the late 90's, Susan was one of the first to receive the prestigious "Lighting Certified" designation from the National Council on Qualifications for the Lighting Professions, and is currently studying to become a Certified Lighting Consultant with the American Lighting Association. While the NCQLP primarily recognizes excellence in the commercial lighting industry, the American Lighting Association is a trade association primarily representing the residential lighting industry. Its membership includes retail showrooms and lighting designers that are dedicated to providing the public with the proper application of quality residential lighting.
Susan has won international lighting awards for major projects such as New Birth Missionary Baptist Church in Lithonia, Georgia, the UPS headquarters in Alpharetta, Georgia, the Marriott Heathrow in Lake Mary, Florida and the Adidas hospitality facility for the 1996 Atlanta Olympics. One of her most exciting current projects is a Southern Living inspired community in Columbus, Georgia that includes homes, apartments, retail, office space and a chapel. But she considers every customer's project, no matter how big or small, to be a unique opportunity to use lighting as a key design element to make their home a special and inviting place.
You can visit Susan in the showroom or make an appointment to have her come to your home and assess your lighting needs in person. With the advent of design websites like Pinterest and Houzz, more customers are realizing the vast array of lighting styles that are available for the home. But many mistakes can be made when ordering from a website that doesn’t allow you to talk with a lighting professional. "Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, this 1906 Greek Revival mansion was originally the Holberg Hotel. The 8,000 square foot Inn with nine guest bedrooms still has its original features: Georgia heart pine floors, ornate tin ceilings, elegant light fixtures and chandeliers, and eleven fireplaces. A beautiful garden, rocking chairs, and porch swings on the generous wrap-around veranda add to your journey back in time.  You’ll also enjoy the Inn’s upstairs library with its hundreds of books and magazines.   You can read in your room, the library or one of the eighteen other rooms and parlors.
Many notable people have been guests at The Veranda. For many years Confederate soldiers held their yearly reunions here; Margaret Mitchell interviewed Confederate Veterans for “Gone With the Wind”; William Jennings Bryan (of the Scopes Trial fame) stayed here in 1908 while running for President. The movie, “Broken Bridges”, was also filmed at The Veranda in 2006."

Senoia PorchFest 2025
‍
Senoia PorchFest is a community-based music event that takes place on residential porches in Senoia! Porches and yards become stages for local and regional bands and musicians. Senoia’s streets become artist galleries and walk-up restaurants. During PorchFest, local musicians or bands set up on selected porches and perform for an hour. The performances can range from solo acts, to full bands, with a wide variety of selected genres.
PorchFest is a FREE event to attend
, organized and sponsored by the Senoia Downtown Development Authority. In addition to the music, PorchFest also includes food vendors, art displays, and kids' activities! PorchFest is a celebration of music, creativity, and community! Come enjoy live performances, support local artists, and Enjoy Senoia with us!

- Reserved Parking
- VIP Bathroom Access (2:00-7:00pm)
- Door Prize Entry to win a basket of spirits valued at $1,000
- Drink Tickets (3) Adult Beverages
- Small Bites
- Commemorative Lanyard
- $15 Gift Card
- Event T-Shirt
- Live Music

PORCHFEST PERFORMANCE SCHEDULE & MAP
‍
Planning on attending PorchFest Senoia? Here’s what you need to know…
PorchFest is a pedestrian event. Last year’s PorchFest was attended by over 5000 music enthusiasts. The streets where PorchFest will take place will be closed to all automobile and golf cart traffic. Attendees are encouraged to park in downtown Senoia and walk to the porches and stages. Walking shoes and folding chairs are recommended. Limited golf cart shuttles will be available to get participants to the PorchFest perimeter, but no transportation will be available within the perimeter of the event.
Volunteers will be available throughout the neighborhoods to answer questions.
Maps of the porches/performers will be posted at intersections.
As you visit each porch and performance, please watch out for plantings in front of homes and plan to sit or stand on lawns, walkways, sidewalks or the closed street.
Please use caution when walking on streets that are not closed to automobiles, golf carts or bicycles.
For additional information please contact porchfestbands@enjoysenoia.com or info@enjoysenoia.com

Event Overview:
Get ready to celebrate the most wonderful time of the year at our annual Light Up Senoia Parade! This cherished tradition brings the community together for an evening of festivities and Christmas cheer! Parade begins promptly at 6:30pm. This is a wonderful way to promote your business and have some holiday fun!
Event Highlights:
Festive Floats by local businesses, schools, churches, and organizations
Dance Groups
Cheerful Music & Holiday Entertainment
Food Trucks
Santa Claus
Santa's Workshop
Main Street Tree Lighting
Awards & Trophies
& More!
Event Schedule:
4:00pm: Santa's Workshop Opens! Located at the Senoia Farmers' Market, 40 Travis Street
‍
4:15pm: Pre parade entertainment begins in front of the stage on Main Street
‍
4:30pm-5:30pm: Check in for parade participants (further details below)
‍
6:00pm: Santa's Workshop Closes, making your way towards Main Street for the parade!
‍
6:30pm: PARADE BEGINS
‍
The Light Up Senoia tree lighting will immediately follow the parade. And then Santa will receive visitors on his sleigh until 8:30.
‍
The theme for the parade this year is
Winter Wonderland
! We encourage you to create your float design with our theme as the primary focus. Floats will be judge in the following categories based on the theme
Winter Wonderland
.
1) Mayor's Trophy (best overall entry)
2) Grand Marshal's Trophy (best creative entry)
3) Santa's Trophy (best Christmas Spirit)
4) Rudolf's Trophy (best lighted entry)
5) Reindeer Trophy (best musical/vocal/dance entry)
‍
With it being nighttime,
we encourage lights
! It will be dark when parade starts, so use those LIGHTS!!! (You will supply all electricity for your entry) Be creative! We do ask that you don’t have Santa on your float as he will be at the end of the parade already!! Please have some type of banner in front of your entry announcing your groups name.
Please
…
no items can be thrown from vehicles
! You may have someone
walking beside your entry to hand out candy, beads etc. This is for the safety of the children. Thank you for your cooperation
.
All Parade Slots have been filled, we are no longer taking registrations for parade participants.
‍
There is a $20 fee for each parade entry. We will send out a confirmation email with your lineup number and check in location to you before parade date.
‍
CHECK IN TIME FOR PARADE PARTICIPANTS BEGINS AT 4:30 AND ENDS AT 5:30!
‍
QUESTIONS OR FURTHER INFO PLEASE CALL or EMAIL:
Jack Martin 404-925-2404, Casey Luschen 706-566-3416, or Steph Reeder 618-559-8997 or email lightupsenoia@enjoysenoia.com

Event Overview....
The Senoia Car Show in Senoia, GA is an annual event that showcases 500 classic and custom cars from all over Georgia. The event takes place in September and features a range of vehicles, including vintage cars, muscle cars, hot rods, and custom trucks. The Senoia Car Show is a family-friendly event that offers something for everyone. In addition to the impressive collection of cars on display, there are also food vendors, music, door prizes and activities for kids.
One of the highlights of the Senoia Car Show is the opportunity to meet and talk with car owners, who are often passionate enthusiasts who are happy to share their knowledge and stories about their vehicles. Many of the cars on display are restored to their original condition, while others have been customized with modern features and modifications.
The event is held in downtown Senoia, which is a charming and historic town located about 30 miles south of Atlanta. Visitors to the Senoia Car Show can explore the town's shops and restaurants, as well as its many historic sites and landmarks.
The Senoia Car Show is a fun and exciting event that celebrates the rich history and culture of the automobile. Whether you're a car enthusiast or just looking for a fun day out with the family, the Senoia Car Show is definitely worth checking out.The show is open to all cars & trucks 25 years and older (1998 and older).

Valve Cover Races - Rules and Regulations
Valve cover racing is a competitive event similar to pinewood derby, but vehicles are made using a valve cover from a car engine rather than a wooden block. Contestants are encouraged to build your own "car" and bring it to the event to race against others. Customization is encouraged per the rules below. The event is open to children and adults of all ages.
‍
Car/Valve Cover Specs
1. Length - up to 30 inches
2. Width - up to 10 inches
3. Height -up to 10 inches
4. Weight - up to 10 pounds
5. No engines or propulsion
6. No moving weights
7. Wheels can be attached to the valve cover in any manner, but must not extend beyond
the front of the valve cover
8. Nothing can extend beyond the front of the valve cover (Car)
9. Cars shall be based on an actual rocker cover from an automobile
10. Cars must have four wheels, each no more than six inches in diameter
‍
The Course
The track will be similar to a Pinewood Derby track. A wooden track with two lanes approximately 20 ft. long and 4ft incline with a single starting gate. Located at the bottom of Main Street during the Senoia Car Show.
The Race
﻿﻿Cars will be run in heats of two cars each
﻿﻿The cars will be launched with the front edge of the valve cover touching the starting gate. The first car to have its front edge cross the finish line will be the winner. If neither car makes it to the finish line, the car going the furthest in its lane wins
﻿﻿Winning cars will advance to the next round until all are eliminated except one car
‍

Senoia PorchFest 2024
Senoia PorchFest is a community-based music event that takes place on residential porches in Senoia! Porches and yards become stages for local and regional bands and musicians. Senoia’s streets become artist galleries and walk-up restaurants. During PorchFest, local musicians or bands set up on selected porches and perform for an hour. The performances can range from solo acts, to full bands, with a wide variety of selected genres.
PorchFest is a FREE event to attend
, organized and sponsored by the Senoia Downtown Development Authority. In addition to the music, PorchFest also includes food vendors, art displays, and kids' activities! PorchFest is a celebration of music, creativity, and community! Come enjoy live performances, support local artists, and Enjoy Senoia with us!
‍
Click here
to view our "Day of PorchFest " map and events including a list of bands, music genres, food vendors and more.
‍
PorchFest Senoia will be held Sunday, September 1st, 2024 from 3:00 PM - 7:00 PM
Attendees will enjoy:
Local and regional musicians and artists
Food trucks & drink proprietors
Kids activities
Optional Pre-Party called Soundcheck Social (2:00 pm - 3:00 pm)
Optional VIP Concert called Twilight Tunes (7:00 pm - 10:00 pm)
All performances are FREE, with tips for the musicians suggested.

VIP Badges will give you access to the Soundcheck Social from 2:00pm - 3:00pm. Includes free beer, wine, and light fare.

Planning on attending PorchFest Senoia? Here’s what you need to know…
PorchFest is a pedestrian event. Last year’s PorchFest was attended by over 2000 music enthusiasts. The streets where PorchFest will take place will be closed to all automobile and golf cart traffic. Attendees are encouraged to park in downtown Senoia and walk to the porches and stages. Walking shoes and folding chairs are recommended. Limited golf cart shuttles will be available to get participants to the PorchFest perimeter, but no transportation will be available within the perimeter of the event.
Volunteers will be available throughout the neighborhoods to answer questions.
Maps of the porches/performers will be posted at intersections.
As you visit each porch and performance, please watch out for plantings in front of homes and plan to sit or stand on lawns, walkways, sidewalks or the closed street.
Please use caution when walking on streets that are not closed to automobiles, golf carts or bicycles.
For additional information please contact

The Senoia Car Show in Senoia, GA is an annual event that showcases 500 classic and custom cars from all over Georgia. The event takes place in September and features a range of vehicles, including vintage cars, muscle cars, hot rods, and custom trucks. The Senoia Car Show is a family-friendly event that offers something for everyone. In addition to the impressive collection of cars on display, there are also food vendors, music, door prizes and activities for kids.
One of the highlights of the Senoia Car Show is the opportunity to meet and talk with car owners, who are often passionate enthusiasts who are happy to share their knowledge and stories about their vehicles. Many of the cars on display are restored to their original condition, while others have been customized with modern features and modifications.
The event is held in downtown Senoia, which is a charming and historic town located about 30 miles south of Atlanta. Visitors to the Senoia Car Show can explore the town's shops and restaurants, as well as its many historic sites and landmarks.
Overall, the Senoia Car Show is a fun and exciting event that celebrates the rich history and culture of the automobile. Whether you're a car enthusiast or just looking for a fun day out with the family, the Senoia Car Show is definitely worth checking out.

Senoia PorchFest 2024
Senoia PorchFest is a community-based music event that takes place on residential porches in Senoia! Porches and yards become stages for local and regional bands and musicians. Senoia’s streets become artist galleries and walk-up restaurants. During PorchFest, local musicians or bands set up on selected porches and perform for an hour. The performances can range from solo acts, to full bands, with a wide variety of selected genres.
PorchFest is a FREE event to attend
, organized and sponsored by the Senoia Downtown Development Authority. In addition to the music, PorchFest also includes food vendors, art displays, and kids' activities! PorchFest is a celebration of music, creativity, and community! Come enjoy live performances, support local artists, and Enjoy Senoia with us!

Attendees will enjoy:
Local and regional musicians and artists

Optional VIP Concert called Twilight Tunes (7:00 pm - 10:00 pm)

Planning on attending PorchFest Senoia? Here’s what you need to know…
PorchFest is a pedestrian event. Last year’s PorchFest was attended by over 2000 music enthusiasts. The streets where PorchFest will take place will be closed to all automobile and golf cart traffic. Attendees are encouraged to park in downtown Senoia and walk to the porches and stages. Walking shoes and folding chairs are recommended. Limited golf cart shuttles will be available to get participants to the PorchFest perimeter, but no transportation will be available within the perimeter of the event.
Volunteers will be available throughout the neighborhoods to answer questions.
Maps of the porches/performers will be posted at intersections.
As you visit each porch and performance, please watch out for plantings in front of homes and plan to sit or stand on lawns, walkways, sidewalks or the closed street.
Please use caution when walking on streets that are not closed to automobiles, golf carts or bicycles.
For additional information please contact

VIP Table Wristbands
If you have purchased a VIP table, you can stop by the Welcome Center at 68 Main Street in downtown Senoia to pick up your VIP table wristbands
beginning on Thursday, May 25th
.  During the week before Memorial Day Weekend, the Welcome Center will be open Tuesday, 05/23, through Friday, 05/26, from 11-3 and on Saturday, 05/27, from 10-4.
Eight (8) wristbands will be provided per VIP table. You will be responsible for distributing wristbands to those sitting at your table. Any VIP ticket purchasers who do not pick up their wristbands before the event can do so at the DDA tent, near the VIP area at the event. You will need either the e-ticket provided via email when you purchased your ticket, or the name, address and contact phone number or email address used when VIP table was purchased online.
Parking
Parking is available in all the public areas of the city, and at the old Ball Fields and Senior Center on Howard Rd.
VIP Golf Cart Parking
For those purchasing VIP Table Bundles with Golf Cart Parking - we have very limited space for golf cart parking in close proximity to the VIP tent area. Last year, we ran out of space due to the large number of 6 and 8 person golf carts and a few side-by-side carts. To ensure fairness for all and and to also ensure we have space for everyone who purchases a golf cart parking pass, we have the following parking restrictions:
‍
Side by Side ATV’s will not be allowed to use VIP golf cart parking.
Golf carts larger than 4 seaters will only be allowed one VIP golf cart parking permit.
VIP golf cart parking will close at 9 pm and not reopen until the firework show is over.
VIP golf cart parking will be accessed via the cart path on Howard Rd and passes will be checked at entry.
‍
VIP Golf Cart parking area is accessed via the cart path on Howard Road adjacent to the old ball fields.
‍
VIP golf cart passes will include your name, the ticket package you purchased, and a QR code that will be scanned when you enter.
‍
Handicap and Sponsor VIP Parking Area
Handicap and Sponsor VIP Parking will be in the library parking lot at 148 Pylant Street, Senoia, GA. Valid passes will be required for entrance. The entrance to Pylant St at GA-16/Wells Street will be closed as will the entrance to Pylant Street at the intersection of Morgan Street, only vendors and valid passes will be allowed.

Most Frequently Asked Questions
Which food trucks will be there?
We have a wide variety of food trucks coming to Memorial Day this year! Lots of options between sweet and savory trucks. So far, these are the food trucks that will be attending our Memorial Day event:
Lisa's Creperie, Curious Pig, Knife and Stone, Lepoma's Pizza, Love at Wurst Sight, Crave BBQ, Kettleworks Popcorn, Little Miss Juicy, Sunset Slush Italian Ice, Mama Fannie's Beignets, and Big Daddy's Peanuts.
‍
I purchased a VIP table, how do I get my VIP Table Wristbands?
If you have purchased a VIP table, you can stop by the Welcome Center at 68 Main Street in downtown Senoia to pick up your VIP table wristbands
beginning on Tuesday, May 23rd.
During the week before Memorial Day Weekend, the Welcome Center will be open Tuesday, 05/23, through Friday, 05/26, from 11-3 and on Saturday, 05/27, from 10-4.
Eight (8) wristbands will be provided per VIP table. You will be responsible for distributing wristbands to those sitting at your table. Any VIP ticket purchasers who do not pick up their wristbands before the event can do so at the DDA tent, near the VIP area at the event. You will need either the e-ticket provided via email when you purchased your ticket, or the name, address and contact phone number or email address used when VIP table was purchased online.
‍
Can I decorate my VIP table?
Yes! You are welcome to bring some patriotic decor for your VIP table.
Can the general public use the park area without purchasing a VIP ticket?
There is a paid VIP area, but the rest of the park is open for the public to enjoy.
Can I bring a cooler or alcoholic beverages?
Coolers are not permitted. Alcoholic beverages may not be brought onto the park grounds.

SOLD OUT!
We're sorry, but this year's Pub Crawl event is sold out, no additional tickets are available.
‍
‍
To all Pub Crawler aficionados:
To spread out the crowd and not overwhelm the staff, we need a shotgun start at different restaurants. When you pick up your t-shirts, we will group you in batches of 5 to 7 and give you a starting destination. No, we will not break up couples, and we recommend you try and meet someone new. A Pub Crawl is a great way to make new friends. On to the next bar! Please maintain a clockwise rotation per the map on the other side of this page to keep you from colliding with the other revelers.
Please remember to tip your server!
The bars will hand out Mardi Gras beads with the drink specials. You may cash in the beads for playing cards at the poker run. Set your alarm to return to Curious Kitchen at 9 p.m. We will line up 10 REVELERS at a time along the long tables and deal out five cards face up.
We are Poker Purists. That means no wild cards, five card stud, and for speed, hole card up. Ten players at a time. The best hand wins the round. For example, with 50 players, that will be 5 rounds and only one round per contestant.
The winner of that round will take a seat alongside the coveted Senoia Pub Crawl Trophy! If the best hand of the next round is better, the new player takes the seat.

Best of 2023 Senoia Car Show
Welcome to the exclusive gallery showcasing the pride and passion of the 2023 Senoia Car Show.
Share this
Welcome to the exclusive gallery showcasing the pride and passion of the 2023 Senoia Car Show. Held in the picturesque and historic downtown streets of Senoia, Georgia, this year's show dazzled with over 500 classic and custom cars, each telling its own unique story of automotive excellence. As you browse through these images, immerse yourself in the artistry and craftsmanship of these exceptional vehicles, all of which have been meticulously maintained or modified to showcase the rich history and culture of the automobile. Join us in celebrating these extraordinary machines and the passionate enthusiasts behind them, who brought life to the 18th Annual Historic Downtown Senoia Car Show.
